title: WAL commit-path bundle: buffer, writer cadence, flush batch, group commit, compression
configuration_cause: wal_buffers=512 (4MB) with wal_writer_delay=200ms and commit_delay=0 leaves commit-path syncs unbatched; wal_wait anomaly persists across both accepted replicates while wal_sync_time_per_txn=1.16ms and sync_average_ms=0.142ms indicate per-commit fsync queueing rather than raw device stall.
mechanism: The wal_commit_path bundle targets commit-path sync frequency and queueing. Raising wal_buffers to 2048 (16MB) absorbs bursts so backends rarely block on WALWrite. Lowering wal_writer_delay to 50ms and wal_writer_flush_after to 64 (512kB) makes the writer flush smaller batches more often, smoothing dirty_bytes spikes (p95 ~102MB) and reducing fsync queue depth. commit_delay=100us with commit_siblings=2 lets concurrent committers coalesce into one fsync when >=2 siblings are active, cutting sync count per txn. wal_compression=on shrinks full-page-image WAL (wal_fpi_per_txn=1.4e-4) reducing bytes per sync. Together these lower wal_waiting_backends and per-commit sync latency, freeing terminal capacity for GetUserTweets.
query_effect: GetUserTweets and InsertTweet commit paths see fewer WAL-write stalls; p99 tail of InsertTweet (2343us) should shrink as fsync queueing drops.
expected_tps_effect: Modest increase (0.5-2%) via reduced commit-path stall on the dominant GetUserTweets terminal; primary value is diagnostic confirmation of the WAL-sync mechanism.
expected_latency_effect: Lower wal_waiting_backends and InsertTweet p99; GetUserTweets p50 roughly unchanged.

predictions.rationale: Larger WAL buffer plus faster writer cadence and group commit reduce backends blocked on WALWrite.
Group commit coalesces fsyncs; compression reduces bytes per sync.
Freed terminal capacity from reduced commit stalls raises completed TPS.

alternatives.statement: If only wal_buffers matters, raising it alone would move wal_waiting_backends while writer cadence knobs stay inert.
If WAL wait is a sampling artifact of idle-in-transaction backends, the bundle leaves wal_waiting_backends unchanged and TPS flat.

why_exceeds_incumbent: Incumbent leaves the wal_wait anomaly unresolved across both accepted replicates; this bundle directly addresses the diagnosed WAL commit-path mechanism with a coherent joint action rather than a single knob.

knob_changes.numerical_basis: 4x current 4MB to 16MB, within safe [512,4096]; absorbs commit bursts.
Reduce from 200ms to 50ms, within safe [20,500]; faster writer wake-up flushes smaller batches.
Halve to 64 (512kB), within safe [0,1024]; smaller flush batches smooth dirty_bytes spikes.
100us collection window, within safe [0,1000]; enables group commit when siblings present.
Lower activation threshold to 2, within safe [0,20]; more committers qualify for group commit.
Enable to shrink full-page-image WAL (wal_fpi_per_txn=1.4e-4), reducing bytes per sync.

nodes.label: Fewer and smaller WAL syncs per commit; less WALWrite queueing

cross_domain_requirements: Restart required for wal_buffers; coordinate with concurrency_maintenance to avoid overlapping restart-class changes.
